title: Russian Jets Zoom Dangerously Close to UK Spy Plane Over the Black Sea!
summary: Imagine you're flying a plane, and suddenly two fighter jets roar up right next to you — so close you could almost wave at the pilots! That's what happened to a British spy plane crew last month over the Black Sea. Two Russian warplanes, a Su-35 and a Su-27, zoomed dangerously close to an unarmed RAF Rivet Joint aircraft. The Su-35 got so near that it triggered the plane's emergency systems and turned off its autopilot. The Su-27 flew past the front of the RAF plane six times, getting as close as six metres (19 feet) from its nose! The UK's Defence Secretary, John Healey, said the Russian pilots' actions were "unacceptable" and created a serious risk of an accident. He praised the RAF crew for their "outstanding professionalism" during the scary flybys. The Rivet Joint was on a normal flight to help protect NATO's eastern side. This isn't the first time something like this has happened. In 2022, a Russian pilot fired a missile at a similar RAF plane over the Black Sea. The UK says this latest incident is the most dangerous since then. Healey said these actions won't stop the UK from defending NATO and its allies. The UK government is worried about more Russian aggression in the area, including recent submarine activity near important underwater cables in the North Sea. So, what do you think? Was this just a warning, or something more serious? One thing's for sure: the skies over the Black Sea are a tense place right now!
why_it_matters: If an accident had started a war by mistake, it could affect fuel prices and safety for families everywhere, even far from the Black Sea.
